clue.text: What may be said on meeting difficult situation?

definitions.text: What may be said on meeting
definitions.meaning: a formal greeting offered when introduced to someone
a 'fine how-d'ye-do' is a muddle or awkward state of affairs

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what greeting suits an awkward first encounter.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a polite formal salutation and, idiomatically, a fuss or awkward predicament.

clue.text: Injure top of head and limb

indicators.note: the top of a word, in a down clue, is its first letter

parts.note: an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: A warning about hurting your head and a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: To injure someone is to do them physical damage, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Fence associated with brilliant crime writer

parts.note: a wall is a kind of fence or barrier
ace is slang for excellent or brilliant

explanation.surface: A receiver of stolen goods teams up with a gifted author of thrillers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fence' tempts as the criminal receiver of stolen goods, fitting the crime surface, but it is a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Wallace was a prolific English writer of thrillers and detective stories, so an example.

clue.text: What a tea drinker often says is a farce?

definitions.text: What a tea drinker often says
definitions.meaning: the habitual phrase when adding an extra spoonful of leaves to the teapot
the title of a Ray Cooney stage farce

explanation.surface: A question about a tea drinker's catchphrase being a comic play.
explanation.definitionFit: The tea-making saying about an extra spoonful is also the title of a well-known British stage comedy.

clue.text: Dress material in orange I'd ordered

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone ordered a dress fabric in orange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like a purchase but tells you to rearrange ORANGE and ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Organdie is a fine, stiff, sheer cotton fabric used for dresses.

clue.text: Tug sunk in river flood

indicators.note: something sunk in a river is placed within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
to lug is to pull or tug

explanation.surface: A tugboat goes down in a river in spate.
explanation.definitionFit: A deluge is a great flood or downpour, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A young woman lacking finish, unfortunately

indicators.note: a word lacking its finish has its final letter dropped

parts.note: a lass is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A girl who sadly never completes things.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an interjection expressing regret, used much like 'sadly'.

clue.text: Greek character holding a dance

indicators.note: one piece holds the other, which sits inside it

parts.note: lambda is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person holding a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' reads as a person, but it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast Brazilian partner dance, so an example.

clue.text: Guard on Hampshire river in trial filming

parts.note: a screen guards or shields
the Test is a chalk-stream river in Hampshire, England

explanation.surface: A security guard stands on a riverbank during a test shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a famous trout river in Hampshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: An audition on camera to judge an actor's suitability for a role is a trial filming.

clue.text: Turned over winner's medal — it's not 22 carat

parts.note: rolled means turned over and over
the gold medal goes to the winner

explanation.surface: A champion flipped their medal and found it was not pure gold.
explanation.definitionFit: This is base metal coated with a thin layer of the precious metal, so not high-carat solid.

clue.text: Ruler from east, on edge going west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A ruler arrives from the east and heads west along a border.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or prince in parts of the Middle East.

clue.text: Borough, region close to Manhattan, is alight

parts.note: a state is a region

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
to alight is to land, as a bird does

explanation.surface: A New York borough near Manhattan is ablaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alight' reads as burning, but it means to come down and settle.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the five boroughs of New York City, so an example.

clue.text: Considerably old Portuguese port

parts.note: far, as in 'far better', means considerably

explanation.surface: A rather old harbour town in Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Faro is a coastal city in the Algarve in southern Portugal.

clue.text: Difficult experience seeing cavalier heading off on horse

indicators.note: with its heading gone, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a cavalier is a mounted knight
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: An ordeal: watching a mounted gallant ride away.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad dream, or figuratively any harrowing ordeal, is a nightmare.

clue.text: Property not supposed to be put on top of car

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits above the next

parts.note: real things are actual, not merely supposed
an estate is a car with a load area behind the seats, a station wagon

explanation.surface: Something not imaginary is placed on a car roof.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate is the British term for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: Land and buildings are property in the legal sense.

clue.text: Charged boy the Parisian court's imprisoned

indicators.note: one piece locks the others up inside it

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name
le is French for the
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A lad charged and locked up by a French court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' reads as accused, but it is the definition in its electrical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something carrying current or an exciting atmosphere is charged.

clue.text: Finally book foremost of trips

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps

indicators.note: the foremost letter of a word is its first

explanation.surface: At last, booking the first of several journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' looks like a verb meaning reserve but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means eventually, after a long wait.

clue.text: Break ranks? Abe Lincoln's here

indicators.note: to break is to smash up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier breaks ranks; Abe Lincoln is present.
explanation.walkthrough: Abe Lincoln suggests the president, but Lincoln here is the state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln is the capital city of this US state, so the state is where that city lies.

clue.text: Picked up stole

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both raised by hand and pilfered.

clue.text: Centre in Telford, not just a pleasure ground

indicators.note: the centre of a seven-letter word is its fourth letter

parts.note: unfair means not just

explanation.surface: A town centre that is no mere pleasure park.
explanation.walkthrough: Telford is a town in Shropshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor amusement park with rides and stalls is a pleasure ground.

clue.text: Most of natural talent displayed on Caribbean island mountain

indicators.note: most of a word drops its last letter

parts.note: a bent is an aptitude or natural talent
Nevis is an island in the Caribbean

explanation.surface: Natural gifts on show on a Caribbean island's peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Nevis, in Scotland, is the highest peak in the British Isles.

clue.text: Disappear after pinching king's shiny coat

indicators.note: one piece pinches the other, holding it inside

parts.note: to vanish is to disappear
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A thief vanishes after stealing the king's glossy coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear glossy finish brushed onto wood is a shiny protective coating.

clue.text: Completely at home, toddler with duck

parts.note: in means at home
a tot is a small child
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: Fully at home with a small child and a pet duck.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means as a whole or entirely.

clue.text: Drink associated with Victorian tramp?

definitions.meaning: an evening alcoholic drink taken at dusk
in Australia, a swagman who turns up at dusk for a meal and bed; Victoria is an Australian state

explanation.definitionFit: It is both an evening tipple and an Australian vagrant, Victorian meaning from Victoria rather than of the era.

clue.text: Painful, my leaving Indian city

indicators.note: a word leaving another is taken out of it

parts.note: Mysore is a city in Karnataka, India
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sorely leaving an Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: A sore spot is one that aches or hurts.

clue.text: Is able to house large family

indicators.note: one piece houses the other inside it

parts.note: can means is able

explanation.surface: Can a big family find a home?
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is an extended family group, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: A practice on the opponents' ground

parts.note: a way is a habit or customary practice

explanation.surface: A training session at the rival team's stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: A team plays away when the fixture is at the other side's venue.

clue.text: Plays with barking Alpine dog

parts.note: to toy with is to play with

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A dog from the Alps fools around, barking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' seems to be the dog's noise, but it means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy spaniel is a small breed of spaniel, so an example of a dog.

clue.text: Organ — new make

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A newly made church organ.
explanation.definitionFit: To make money is to earn it, as in 'make a living'.

clue.text: Sometimes won hand with ten, after twisting

indicators.note: twisting means turning the letters round into a new order

explanation.surface: Occasionally a card player wins a hand with a ten after twisting.
explanation.walkthrough: In pontoon, 'twist' asks for another card, fitting the card surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means occasionally, from time to time.
